account:
Today has mostly followed ordinary town business: morning correspondence, a market walk, lunch at home, and now the one o'clock accounts review. The builder is here to report on a bridge inspection and provide an itemized repair estimate; no defects have yet been confirmed, and I authorized inspection only, not spending or alterations. The secretary is here, as is freight, whose business I have not yet heard.

The only slightly unusual news concerns the bakery. Townsfolk Ten reported the baker carrying a sack of bread at the bridge around ten thirty-five, and the secretary independently saw the baker near the bridge with bread around ten thirty-six. Neither established the baker's destination or a companion. The neighbour mentioned reports of bakery lights, but without details establishing unusual hours or activity. The baker reportedly said fresh bread was coming to market and knew of no special occasion. These observations could simply reflect ordinary baking and deliveries; I have no evidence of a shortage, secret gathering, or wrongdoing. The secretary has received no reports of shortages or unusual evening activity.

I remain curious rather than convinced anything covert is happening. The neighbour has promised to mention anything personally observed along the docks at our three o'clock tea at the east-bank cottage. For now, I should hear the builder's actual findings and attend to the accounts rather than turn uncertain bakery gossip into a supposed problem.
